nodes.label: HAG-54 Report: Chef-Kitchen Slice Dead-Button Audit
nodes.rationale: 0 of 12 files had any alert()/confirm()/prompt() stub or not-implemented handler, so no rewiring was needed; every control already called a live endpoint through the shared client. The one real 501-write gap found (POST /inventory/purchases, /inventory/stock, /inventory/stock-action plus the console.log-only handleSaveMaster in InventoryFlow.jsx) was deliberately left untouched because it lives outside the assigned 12 files, is only reachable through the unrouted pages/InventoryPage.jsx, and its backend half is also 501 - the fix belongs to the backend owner rather than a frontend swap. The /inventory/menu-list and /inventory/menu-items endpoints are misleading names: they return the raw stock-item array, while the actual menu-dish shape comes from /restaurant/menu, which the two inventory menu pages correctly call.

nodes.label: src/api.js (shared HTTP client)
nodes.rationale: Client-side HTTP layer reused unchanged across every slice (baseURL '/api', Bearer token from localStorage); its 401 interceptor clears the token and redirects, which is what made the unmount guard on Reports.jsx fetchSummary necessary so summary cards would not be computed from a session that no longer exists. Verified correct by the restaurant slice: every read returns 401 {'message':'No token provided'} without a token and 200 with one, exactly middleware behaviour.

nodes.label: Vite dev proxy 127.0.0.1:5173 -> backend 127.0.0.1:5002
nodes.rationale: Standard test path for every slice: the live backend at 127.0.0.1:5002 is reached through the Vite dev server at 127.0.0.1:5173 with a real admin session - the same route the browser takes. Neither server was restarted during verification; when both were down (HAG-54 hotel-core), endpoint behaviour was verified directly against the backend instead.

nodes.label: components/Inventory/InventoryFlow.jsx (501-write controls)
nodes.rationale: POSTs to three endpoints that return HTTP 501 {'message':'Not implemented yet'}: POST /inventory/purchases (line 1436, closest real match is POST /inventory/purchase-orders which works), POST /inventory/stock (line 1446, no close match), and POST /inventory/stock-action (line 1456, no close match). A fourth handler, handleSaveMaster (line 1465), makes no call at all - it console.logs and fires a success toast - which is a genuine dead control. Left untouched because it is outside the chef-kitchen file set, reachable only through the unrouted pages/InventoryPage.jsx, and the backend half is also 501, so the fix belongs to the backend owner (HAG-2), not a frontend swap.
